proof.observed: 0 misses in 160 runs: chromium 40/40 no diagram + 20/20 no worker, iphone 20/20, webkit 40/40, firefox 40/40. Not a failure under the architect's rule. The miss does occur with a mermaid block whose worker is held (2 misses in 45 chromium runs, the first landing only). The scroll timeline shows the cause, which is not new in this PR. On load, VersionView mounts its editor 2-3 times in every shape, the no-diagram one included. Each mount calls focusMark, and the page collapses to 720 px between mounts. In a miss, the last scrollIntoView ran before the final editor's content was laid out, so the page stayed at its top. With a diagram waiting, the re-run after the diagrams draw repairs it.
proof.negativeControl: The same scratch file with a held worker missed: toBeInViewport 'viewport ratio 0' for 15 s (1 of 20, then 1 of 25, in chromium). So the row can detect a miss.
